brief: Fresh blind judge on reports/packs/prose-tics-r4/ (15 trials). Dispatched as a fresh judge; on arrival I found the pack has ALREADY been judged twice (status judge-prose-r4.json, state=done) and that the mandatory RI-MTH03 M5 second pass is recorded as OWED AND NOT RUN. I run M5.
role: blind judge, third pass, M5 harsher-lens
contamination_control_declared_before_re: HARD BAN: I will not open any t*/answer.md. The predecessor status file's summary block (read while orienting) states the FIRST judge picked reference on 15/15. Therefore every existing answer.md PICK line is a direct answer key. Reading one would void this pass.
HARD BAN: I will not open reports/packs/prose-tics-r4.reveal/ until all 15 of my rows are on disk.
HARD BAN: I will not open reports/packs/prose-tics-r4-judgement.md (the second judge's running record) until after reveal.
HARD BAN: I will not read past the summary preview of orchestration/status/judge-prose-r4.json, and not corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/W1-PROSE-BLIND-r1.md, until after reveal.
I will not open t*/pack.json (carries a_words/b_words) until after my 15 rows are written.
I read ONLY t*/A.txt, t*/B.txt and t01-books/PROMPT.md before answering.

KNOWN RESIDUAL CONTAMINATION, declared up front: I know from the status summary that judge 1 scored 15/15 on provenance and judge 2 scored 15/15 on provenance. That is a base-rate prior that the reference side IS distinguishable. It does not tell me WHICH side in any single trial. It does mean my own accuracy cannot be read as an independent replication of 'is this pack decidable' - only as an independent replication of WHICH side is which.
I write my answers to JUDGEMENT-judge-prose-r4-m5.md, NOT into the existing answer.md files, so the pre-existing record stays byte-untouched.

m3_commit_before_reveal.note: All 15 PROV/QUAL rows, the M5 pass and the WEAKEST POINT existed on disk at this hash BEFORE prose-tics-r4.reveal/ was opened. Sections after this point are appended post-reveal, so the file's later hash will differ by design; this hash is the auditable pre-reveal one.

result.qual_axis_which_side_is_the_better_writi: preferred OURS 15/15 -> RI-MTH03 SsE picked-ours on every row
result.m5_harsher_lens: run; did not overturn a single row; produced a real gap (see below)
result.chance_baseline: 7.5/15 by coin-flip; but effective independent trials ~3 (one per register) because each side is one author, so quote 1-in-8, not 1-in-270
result.headline_defect: R0 LEAK: raw count of [NAME-n] tokens, higher side = reference, scores 15/15 with zero reading and zero domain knowledge. Margins 1.6x-7x, median ~3.5x. This is round 1's failure (a rule counting Vvardenfell scored 17/17) reappearing inside the masking machinery installed to fix it. The README's own check verified what the mask CONTAINS, not how many tokens it ADDS.
other_defects: D1 the PICK: line cannot express the pack's question - provenance and quality point opposite ways on most trials; the two prior judges did not disagree about a single passage, they answered different questions and it was recorded as a 14-row disagreement
D2 pack is no longer blind-safe - two judges' answer.md files sit inside the trial dirs and judge 1 was 15/15, so they are a plaintext answer key in the file the PROMPT tells a judge to write
D3 every PROMPT.md in r4 points at ../prose-tics-r2.reveal/ - a different pack's key - and is headed 'round 2'
D4 trials are not independent - one author per side, so 15 trials carry roughly 3 trials of information

D5 masker over-fires on sentence-initial capitals (nevertheless, finally, perhaps, however all became [NAME-n]) and leaks sentence-initial proper nouns on both sides (gro-Kharbush, gro-Bagrat, Eraamion on ref; Vaskh on ours)
result.gap_for_the_builder: Our prose is monotonous across documents: nine of fifteen passages share one narrator's idiolect. No unreliable narrator, no propagandist, no bore. Measure cross-document voice variance, not just within-document tics.
result.rules_i_pre_declared_that_FAILED: R2 alphabetical sortedness 9/15 (chance), R3 extraction-damage heuristic 5/15 (worse than chance). Reported as plainly as the hit.

could_not_do: Not a clean instrument: I learned judge 1's aggregate 15/15 while orienting, before judging. Declared up front, not discovered after.

M5 literally requires a DIFFERENT fresh agent from the one whose pick was ours; both prior judges are gone, so I ran the harsher lens myself in the same pass. Weaker than the protocol wants and reported as such.

Did not run tools/check-prose.mjs or tools/prose/tic-detector.mjs self-tests - builder instruments, and per rule 4 a pass from them is worthless unless broken first, which I had no budget for. So the cross-document-variance recommendation is UNTESTED against what the tic detector may already do.
Did not open or reconcile against the two existing answer.md sets (they are the answer key); aggregate comparison taken from judge-prose-r4.json, not from the files.
sibling_packs_finding: The orchestrator records TWO W1-PROSE-TICS packs awaiting a round-2 judge. File state confirms prose-tics-r2/ and prose-tics-r3/ have ZERO answer.md files with a PICK: line. But NEITHER should be judged: prose-tics-r3/ carries its own SUPERSEDED.md ('do not judge this pack') because ~380 dialogue lines were rewritten after it was built, and prose-tics-r2/ is the unmasked pack whose leak is already documented and whose corpus r4 supersedes. RECOMMEND closing both as superseded rather than spending judges on prose that is not in the game. prose-tics-voice-r2/ IS answered (5/5 have PICK:).
next_step: None. Judgement written, revealed, scored, banked. Builder action: equalise [NAME-n] token counts across arms (or re-name rather than redact) and assert it fail-closed in the pack builder; move answers to a sibling <pack>.answers/<judge-id>/; fix the stale reveal path in PROMPT.md.
